name: Ouadi Qadisha (the Holy Valley) and the Forest of the Cedars of God (Horsh Arz el-Rab)
description: Carved into the mountains of northern Lebanon, the Qadisha, or Holy Valley, is a deep gorge where Christian monks built hermitages and monasteries into steep cliffs, some of them very old. Above it, near Bsharre, grows a remnant grove of the Cedars of God, last survivors of the vast forests that supplied timber across the ancient world and are mentioned in the Epic of Gilgamesh.
